analysis.title: The Point for North America, Monday 26 October 2026
key_insights: Citi's Washington contacts expect Democrats to retake the House in the midterms while the Senate is too close to call. Divided government likely brings friction, with possible bipartisan areas in permitting reform, some industrial and tax policy, and housing affordability.

Citi industrials team thinks major data center legislation is unlikely to be enacted given Presidential opposition. Tariff policy is likely to stay in flux, with Congress possibly trying to rein in Executive authority while the President stays committed to tariffs.

US Leisure: affordability, not a uniform pullback in discretionary spending, separates winners from losers. Towable RV and boat payments remain well above their historical share of buyer income, while motorcycle and ORV payments are up but outpaced by income growth.

Skydance (SKYD) coverage resumed at Buy with a $10 target. Citi's 2027-2029 EBITDA forecast is below management's internal goals but about 12% above Street estimates, based on $8B of cost synergies by 2029, about $2B above management targets.

Biotech SCLC dinner with Dr. Herzberg: tarlatamab could establish T-cell engagement as a frontline backbone, and DLL3 ADCs could replace chemotherapy in induction or serve as upfront combination partners. Both zoci and IDE849 were viewed positively, with differentiation depending on durability, cumulative safety and compatibility with tarlatamab.

Summit Therapeutics: HARMONi-GI1 showed a 0.75 OS HR and 0.61 PFS HR for ivo in first-line biliary cancer. Only 13 of 63 sites overlap with HARMONi-6's 50 sites, which supports the independence of the results and the case for generalizable PD-1/VEGF benefit.

IDEAYA's IDE849 reported a 17.4-month 2L median OS, 6.9-month median PFS and 60.8% cORR in 2L. Preliminary global safety showed 5% Gr3+ TRAEs at 2.4 mg/kg versus 22.2% at 3.5 mg/kg, with a global update due around YE26 or early 2027.
Zai Lab's zoci+atezo showed about 82% progression-free at 6 months, pointing to a mature mPFS in the high single to low double digits months versus roughly 5 months for standard of care.
Arcus: LITESPARK-012 triplet had about 51% discontinuation for any study drug versus about 36% in control, which Citi says highlights the tolerability advantage of RCUS's cas+ipi+nivo in PEAK-20.

Zymeworks licensed ZW209 (DLL3xCD3xCD28 trispecific) to Roche for $55M upfront and $40M on Ph1b initiation, with up to $718M in further milestones and high-single-digit to mid-teen royalties. Management's call is October 27 at 8:30am ET.
Arrivent's ARR-217 CDH17 ADC beat Citi's roughly 30% ORR bar in mCRC with a 44.8% ORR and 37.9% cORR at 6 mg/kg (N=29). Citi sees a potential registrational path with bevacizumab versus Lonsurf+bev.

First Citizens 3Q26 beat expectations on growth and NIM. The 2027 guide is NII up mid-to-high single digits and a NIM in the mid 3.20s for 4Q27, modestly better than Citi's prior 3.22%. TP raised to $2,500 (+$200).

PulteGroup: Citi cut FY26 EPS about 7% after a 3Q miss and lower deliveries guide. Sept and Oct demand slowed sharply, 4Q guide implies about 50bp of sequential gross margin compression, rating stays Neutral and TP rises to $127.

Packaging Corp of America: it has captured substantially all of the first +$50/ton increase and about half of the second +$50/ton. The +$70/ton hike mostly lands in 1Q27, October bookings are up a little more than 5%, and capacity could reach about 5.9mmt in 2027.

Qiagen agreed to be acquired by EQT for EUR 46.50 per share (about $52) in cash, a 40.3% premium to the unaffected price and EUR 10.8B enterprise value. Citi stays Neutral and raises the target to $52 from $45, with closing expected by mid-2027.
SouthState and Popular 3Q26 reviews: SSB guided NIM of 3.75-3.85% through FY27, above investor expectations, with TP trimmed to $124. BPOP credit is normalizing and TP moves to $193.

Booz Allen FY2Q27 adjusted EPS of $1.76 beat the $1.49 consensus but revenue of $2.78B missed $2.81B and organic growth guidance was cut. FCF yield is about 9.5% and some bulls argue this was the last guidance cut. Citi is sympathetic but notes the argument has failed before. TP raised to $88.

Essential Properties: 2026E AFFO/share falls to $2.03 from $2.04 and 2027E to $2.14 from $2.16. TP cut to $30 from $36 (about 14x forward AFFO) on a more challenged cost of capital and slower capital deployment.
Press reports of an 80,000-site SpaceX build point to a possible fourth national carrier. Citi sees tower companies possibly gaining and telco operators facing strain.

Two serious PHP vulnerabilities pushed cybersecurity stocks. Citi sees reinforced demand for run-time security, web security protections, exposure management and automated pen-testing, but not a spend catalyst for classic vulnerability management players.
US Machinery week 1 earnings wrap-up: Citi expects North America rental company capex to grow mid-to-high single digits in 2026-2028.

PULSE Monitor: confidence was shaken by the debt and equity issuance needed to finance the datacenter buildout, with credit cracks last week and megacap reports highlighting equity supply. The market is punishing both AI spenders and beneficiaries, with a flight to safety (Defensives +8.2%, Growth -4.5% QTD) and the index flat QTD.

PULSE: it is too early to tell if this is an AI-trade inflection or an unwind of stretched positioning. Hyperscaler 3Q reports next week could stabilize sentiment if strong cloud revenue growth continues.

Metal Matters after LME Week: participants were cautious on near-term risks. Citi is more bullish than 2027 consensus on aluminium, near-term copper and lead, more bearish than consensus on zinc, and calls aluminium a dangerous short. It suggests insuring against binary conflict risks most acute this coming week, and turning optimistic if a US-Iran deal materializes by year-end.

US Economics: October PMI remained solid and in line with consensus after September's unexpected increase pushed Treasury yields higher. The market question is whether the AI-dependent expansion continues.

Global Macro Strategy: risk-off is showing up across assets from AI financing worries, French fiscal concerns and high energy prices. Citi holds oil and France hedges, has less AI exposure, adds a USDJPY vol position where vols look low, and goes long Gilts and Bonos versus short France.

Foreign flows: August foreign demand for US corporates and USTs was strong, extending a 21-month streak of strong overseas corporate bond bids, but high-frequency data suggest foreign corporate demand tapered significantly in September. Japanese overseas bond selling persisted four straight weeks since mid-September.

PulteGroup 3Q26 reported a miss and lowered the FY26 deliveries guide. Citi cut FY26 EPS estimate about 7%. 4Q gross margin guidance is 24.0-24.5%, about 50bp lower sequentially.
Packaging Corp of America reported strong 3Q26 results. Legacy shipments were down 0.5%, October bookings are up a little more than 5%, and price increases flow through 4Q26 and 1Q27.
First Citizens 3Q26 reported better than Citi expected. 2027 guide: NII up mid-to-high single digits and 4Q27 NIM in the mid 3.20s.
SouthState 3Q26 reported little change to PPNR outlook. NIM guided to 3.75-3.85% through FY27, fee income assumptions lowered.
Popular 3Q26 reported slightly better than expected apart from credit, which showed modest deterioration from an above-average base.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong cloud revenue growth posted in 2Q could continue in hyperscaler 3Q reports next week and stabilize sentiment.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is punishing both spenders and spend beneficiaries on the debt and equity issuance needed for the datacenter buildout, with credit cracks and a flight to defensives.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler 3Q reports next week failing to show follow-through on strong cloud revenue growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Bulls argue this was the last cut to guidance, with robust FCF yield and accelerating multi-year revenue growth in cybersecurity.
tension_points.bear_case: The last-cut argument has been made unsuccessfully many times this cycle, revenue missed and organic growth guidance was reduced.

tension_points.bull_case: A divided government may find bipartisan compromise on permitting reform, industrial and tax policy, and housing affordability.
tension_points.bear_case: Divided government likely brings meaningful friction, data center legislation is unlikely to pass and tariff policy stays in flux.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Senate outcome different from the expected split, since the Senate is described as too close to call.
